title: Heterologous prime-boost vaccination against H5 avian influenza: Safety and immunogenicity of a MF59-adjuvanted, cell-culture derived H5N6 vaccine.
abstract: With increasing H5 avian influenza cases reported globally and the potential for pandemic emergence, induction of cross-reactive antibody responses may represent an important attribute of an effective vaccine. This phase 2 extension study evaluated immunogenicity and safety of MF59-adjuvanted, cell culture-derived H5N6 vaccine (aH5N6c) in adults primed with MF59-adjuvanted, cell culture-derived H5N1 vaccine (aH5N1c) and in unprimed adults. Adults previously primed with two doses of aH5N1c in the parent study V89_18 were randomized to receive two aH5N6c doses (Group 1) or one aH5N6c and one placebo (Group 2) 3 weeks apart. Unprimed adults received two aH5N6c doses (Group 3). Immunogenicity was assessed by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and microneutralization (MN) assays against the priming (H5N1) and booster (H5N6) strains on Days 1, 8, 22, 43, and 202. Among 258 exposed participants, primed subjects (Groups 1 and 2) showed higher HI geometric mean titers against both strains than unprimed (Group 3) subjects, with MN responses similarly enhanced. Heterologous H5N1 responses were robust in primed subjects (Day 43 HI GMTs: 333-343; seroconversion rates >89%) but minimal in unprimed subjects, with responses persisting to Day 202. Solicited adverse events were mild or moderate, comparable between groups, and consistent with other MF59-adjuvanted pandemic vaccines; no vaccine-related serious adverse events occurred. Heterologous H5N6 booster vaccination in H5N1-primed adults elicited strong cross-reactive immunity against the priming strain, demonstrating long-lasting immune memory for at least 6 y and supporting heterologous prime-boost strategies for pandemic preparedness against emerging H5 outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the urgent public-health need to prepare for potential H5 avian influenza pandemics by evaluating whether heterologous prime-boost vaccination could induce cross-reactive antibody responses against antigenically distinct H5 strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This phase 2 extension study enrolled adults previously primed with two doses of MF59-adjuvanted, cell culture-derived H5N1 vaccine and randomized them to receive two H5N6 vaccine doses, one H5N6 dose plus placebo, or two H5N6 doses in unprimed adults.
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was measured by hemagglutination inhibition and microneutralization assays against both the priming H5N1 and booster H5N6 strains on Days 1, 8, 22, 43, and 202; safety was monitored for solicited adverse events.
analysis.main_results: Among 258 exposed participants, primed subjects showed higher HI geometric mean titers against both strains than unprimed subjects, with seroconversion rates exceeding 89% in primed groups and responses persisting to Day 202; solicited adverse events were mild to moderate and no vaccine-related serious adverse events occurred.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the robust heterologous H5N1 responses in primed adults as evidence of durable immune memory lasting at least six years, highlighting the potential of heterologous prime-boost strategies for pandemic preparedness against emerging H5 outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of heterologous H5N6 boosting in H5N1-primed populations to rapidly broaden cross-reactive immunity, informing pandemic vaccine deployment and surveillance strategies for H5 avian influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s single-centre design, limited follow-up duration, and absence of a licensed comparator limit generalisability and long-term safety assessment, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 2 extension trial evaluated immunogenicity and safety of an MF59-adjuvanted, cell culture-derived H5N6 vaccine in adults previously primed with an MF59-adjuvanted H5N1 vaccine and in unprimed adults. Heterologous boosting produced higher hemagglutination inhibition and microneutralization titers against both H5N1 and H5N6 strains in primed participants, with seroconversion rates above 89% and responses persisting for at least six months. Unprimed participants showed minimal responses. Solicited adverse events were mild to moderate and no vaccine-related serious adverse events occurred. The authors conclude that heterologous prime-boost vaccination elicits strong cross-reactive immunity and durable immune memory, supporting its use in pandemic preparedness for emerging H5 outbreaks.

abstract_zh: 随着全球报告的 H5 禽流感 病例的增加以及出现大流行的可能性,交叉反应性抗体反应的诱导可能代表了有效 疫苗 的一个重要属性。这项 2 期扩展研究评估了 MF59 佐剂、细胞培养物衍生的 H5N6 疫苗 (aH5N6c) 在用 MF59 佐剂、细胞培养物衍生的 H5N1 疫苗 (aH5N1c) 免疫的成人和未免疫成人中的免疫原性和安全性。先前在母研究 V89_18 中接受过两剂 aH5N1c 的成年人被随机接受两剂 aH5N6c 剂量(第 1 组)或一剂 aH5N6c 和一剂安慰剂(第 2 组),间隔 3 周。未接种疫苗的成年人接受两剂 aH5N6c 剂量(第 3 组)。在第 1、8、22、43 和 202 天,通过针对初免(H5N1)和加强(H5N6)菌株的血凝抑制(HI)和微中和(MN)测定来评估免疫原性。在 258 名暴露参与者中,初免受试者(第 1 组和第 2 组)对两种菌株的 HI 几何平均滴度高于未初免受试者(第 3 组)受试者,并有 MN 反应同样增强。异源 H5N1 反应在初免受试者中表现强劲(第 43 天 HI GMT:333-343;血清转化率 >89%),但在未初免受试者中反应最小,反应持续到第 202 天。所引起的不良事件为轻度或中度,组间可比,并且与其他 MF59 佐剂的流行病 疫苗 一致;没有发生与 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。H5N1 引发的成人中的异源 H5N6 加强剂 疫苗接种 引发了针对引发菌株的强烈交叉反应免疫,证明了至少 6 年的持久免疫记忆,并支持针对新出现的 H5 暴发 的大流行防范的异源引发加强策略。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项 2 期扩展研究招募了之前接受过两剂 MF59 佐剂、细胞培养物衍生的 H5N1 疫苗 的成年人,并将他们随机分配接受两剂 H5N6 疫苗、一剂 H5N6 加安慰剂,或未接受注射的成年人接受两剂 H5N6。
analysis_zh.methods: 在第 1、8、22、43 和 202 天,通过针对初免 H5N1 和加强 H5N6 毒株的血凝抑制和微量中和测定来测量免疫原性;对引起的不良事件进行安全性监测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 258 名暴露的参与者中,与未接触过的受试者相比,接触过的受试者对两种菌株表现出更高的 HI 几何平均滴度,接触过的受试者的血清转化率超过 89%,并且反应持续到第 202 天;引起的不良事件为轻度至中度,没有发生与 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将初免成人中强烈的异源 H5N1 反应解释为持续至少六年的持久免疫记忆的证据,强调了异源初免-加强策略在针对新出现的 H5 暴发 的大流行防范方面的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持在 H5N1 引发的人群中使用异源 H5N6 增强剂来快速扩大交叉反应免疫力,为大流行 疫苗 部署和针对 H5 禽流感 的 监测 策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的单中心设计、有限的随访时间以及缺乏许可的比较器限制了普遍性和长期安全性评估,需要对证据有一定的信心。

title: A bivalent inactivated influenza vaccine incorporating epitope-optimized surface proteins confers cross-protective immunity against H9N2 influenza virus.
abstract: Abstract The H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) has caused substantial economic losses to the global poultry industry and poses a zoonotic threat to humans. Vaccination constitutes a pivotal strategy for the prevention and control of H9N2 AIVs. However, the ongoing antigenic evolution of the virus poses a persistent challenge to the protective efficacy of existing vaccines. Therefore, the development of a broadly protective H9N2 influenza vaccine capable of eliciting cross-reactive immune responses is crucial for mitigating both the disease burden and the risk of pandemics. Here, we developed a bivalent chimeric inactivated vaccine, designated cHANA, by combining two individually rescued chimeric inactivated viruses, cHANA1 and cHANA2. Each recombinant virus carries one set of Epigraph-designed HA and NA immunogens, and the two sets were computationally optimized from global H9N2 HA and NA sequence datasets to complement each other in epitope coverage across the H9N2 viral population. Compared to the WHO-recommended candidate vaccine virus (CVV), AL/39, cHANA elicited more potent cross-reactive antibody responses and T cell immunity in mice. Furthermore, it elicited effective cross-protection against lethal challenge with heterologous H9N2 virus and significantly reduced pulmonary viral loads of mice. By conferring broad protective immunity, this vaccine represents a promising universal candidate for controlling H9N2 outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a broadly protective vaccine against H9N2 avian influenza virus, which has caused economic losses in poultry and poses a zoonotic threat. The researchers created a bivalent chimeric inactivated vaccine, cHANA, by combining two recombinant viruses with epitope-optimized HA and NA immunogens. The vaccine was tested in mice and showed more potent cross-reactive antibody and T cell responses compared to the WHO-recommended candidate vaccine virus, AL/39. It also provided effective cross-protection against lethal challenge with heterologous H9N2 viruses and reduced pulmonary viral loads. These results suggest that cHANA could be a promising universal vaccine candidate for controlling H9N2 outbreaks. The study's findings are supported by direct comparisons in a relevant animal model, though the results may not fully apply to humans.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决 H9N2 禽流感 病毒的持续抗原 进化 带来的挑战,该挑战破坏了现有 疫苗 的有效性。H9N2 禽流感 病毒给全球家禽业造成了重大经济损失,并对人类构成人畜共患威胁。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一种二价嵌合灭活病毒 疫苗,命名为 cHANA,是通过结合两种单独拯救的嵌合灭活病毒 cHANA1 和 cHANA2 开发的。该研究评估了 疫苗 在小鼠中对抗异源 H9N2 病毒致死攻击的功效。
elements_zh.methods: 疫苗 是通过计算优化来自全球 H9N2 序列数据集的 HA 和 NA 免疫原而构建的。每种重组病毒都携带一组 Epigraph 设计的 HA 和 NA 免疫原,这两组免疫原经过优化,可在 H9N2 病毒群体的表位覆盖范围上相互补充。
elements_zh.main_results: 与 WHO 推荐的候选 疫苗 病毒 (CVV)、AL/39 相比,cHANA 在小鼠体内引发了更有效的交叉反应抗体反应和 T 细胞免疫。它还引发了针对异源 H9N2 病毒致命攻击的有效交叉保护,并显着降低了小鼠的肺部病毒载量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,chHANA 疫苗 增强了针对 H9N2 流感病毒的交叉反应免疫力,这是开发针对这种不断进化的病原体的广泛保护性 疫苗 的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,chHANA 可能是一种有前途的通用 疫苗 候选药物,用于控制 H9N2 暴发,通过降低人畜共患 传播 的风险,为家禽业和公共卫生带来潜在益处。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于小鼠模型,结果可能无法完全转化为人类。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它直接将 疫苗 的功效与 WHO 推荐的候选药物进行比较,并在相关动物模型中证明了交叉保护。

title: Genetic evolution, phylodynamics, geographic spread of H9N2 avian influenza viruses in China from 2014 to 2025: an increasing potential zoonotic risk.
abstract: Subtype H9N2 of the avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a growing threat to the poultry industry and public health. However, since 2014, there has been no systematic study of its genetic evolution, genotype, spatial dynamics, and pathogenicity in China. Therefore, we performed a large-scale sequence analysis of the genome of Chinese H9N2 viruses from 2014 to 2025 using public databases and laboratory isolates. We identified 52 different genotypes in 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 4 previously recognized genotypes (G6, G57, G58, and G68) and 48 newly defined genotypes (G118-G163) in this study. G57 and G118 were the main epidemic genotypes in China from 2014 to 2025. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis showed that there were 12 obvious migration paths for the spread of H9N2 AIVs in China from 2017 to 2022. In particular, the South China region was the main transmission centre. H9N2 AIV continues to circulate in chickens and ducks in China and spreads to other hosts. The H9N2 AIVs with the G57 and G118 genotypes could effectively replicate in MDCK, CEF, A549, and HBE cells with titres of 0.97-8.5 lgTCID 50 /mL. The G57 and G118 genotypes H9N2 viruses preferentially bound to α-2,6-linked sialic acid glycopolymers (human receptors), and effectively replicate in multiple organs of mice and chickens and cause pathological changes in the lungs. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and prevention of H9N2 AIVs in China.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Subtype H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a growing threat to poultry and public health, yet systematic analyses of its genetic evolution, genotype dynamics, spatial spread, and pathogenicity in China since 2014 were lacking.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed a large-scale sequence analysis of H9N2 AIV genomes from China spanning 2014 to 2025, integrating public databases and laboratory isolates.
analysis.methods: Genome sequences were retrieved and analyzed to define genotypes and perform Bayesian phylogeographic analysis to reconstruct migration paths and transmission centres.
analysis.main_results: A total of 52 genotypes were identified among 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 48 newly defined genotypes (G118–G163), with G57 and G118 as the main epidemic genotypes. Bayesian analysis revealed 12 migration paths and identified South China as the main transmission centre.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the predominance of G57 and G118 genotypes and their expanded host range as evidence of increasing zoonotic potential, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for H9N2 AIV in China, particularly in South China, to mitigate zoonotic and poultry industry risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on publicly available sequences and laboratory isolates, which may underrepresent geographic and temporal diversity, limiting generalisability and introducing sampling bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 1,591 H9N2 avian influenza virus genomes from China (2014–2025) to characterize genetic evolution, genotype diversity, and spatial spread. Fifty-two genotypes were identified, including 48 newly defined (G118–G163), with G57 and G118 dominating circulation. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis revealed 12 migration paths and designated South China as the principal transmission hub. The authors highlight the increasing zoonotic potential of G57 and G118 genotypes, which showed expanded host range and human receptor binding affinity. The study underscores the need for strengthened surveillance and prevention measures in China, particularly in high-risk regions.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the predominance of G57 and G118 genotypes and their expanded host range as evidence of increasing zoonotic potential, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for H9N2 AIV in China, particularly in South China, to mitigate zoonotic and poultry industry risks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on publicly available sequences and laboratory isolates, which may underrepresent geographic and temporal diversity, limiting generalisability and introducing sampling bias.

title_zh: 2014年至2025年中国H9N2 进化病毒的基因进化、系统动力学、地理传播:潜在人畜共患病风险不断增加。
source_body_en: Subtype H9N2 of the avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a growing threat to the poultry industry and public health. However, since 2014, there has been no systematic study of its genetic evolution, genotype, spatial dynamics, and pathogenicity in China. Therefore, we performed a large-scale sequence analysis of the genome of Chinese H9N2 viruses from 2014 to 2025 using public databases and laboratory isolates. We identified 52 different genotypes in 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 4 previously recognized genotypes (G6, G57, G58, and G68) and 48 newly defined genotypes (G118-G163) in this study. G57 and G118 were the main epidemic genotypes in China from 2014 to 2025. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis showed that there were 12 obvious migration paths for the spread of H9N2 AIVs in China from 2017 to 2022. In particular, the South China region was the main transmission centre. H9N2 AIV continues to circulate in chickens and ducks in China and spreads to other hosts. The H9N2 AIVs with the G57 and G118 genotypes could effectively replicate in MDCK, CEF, A549, and HBE cells with titres of 0.97-8.5 lgTCID 50 /mL. The G57 and G118 genotypes H9N2 viruses preferentially bound to α-2,6-linked sialic acid glycopolymers (human receptors), and effectively replicate in multiple organs of mice and chickens and cause pathological changes in the lungs. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and prevention of H9N2 AIVs in China.

Thursday, August 06, 2026 Australia: H5 Positive Bird Count Rises (n=123) - Victoria Reports 1st Land bird Infection & Investigating Dead Seal #19,280 While not unexpected, overnight CSIRO has reported the first Australian land bird - a Magpie from Victoria - has been confirmed infected with HPAI H5N1. This is their first non-seabird report since the virus was confirmed in June. 6 August 2026 Attributable to Acting Australian Chief Veterinary Officer, Dr Sam Hamilton: Testing at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness (ACDP) has confirmed a further 16 positive detections in Victoria, 14 greater crested terns, one silver gull and one magpie. All of these birds were found in the vicinity of Portland and Nelson. There have also been 6 further confirmed positive detections in South Australia, all in greater crested terns. This includes 1 in Beachport, 1 in Port Vincent, 1 at Pullen Island Port Elliott, 1 in Kangaroo Island,1 in Southend, and 1 in Pelican Point in the lower south east. There have now been 123 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu in Australia, based on samples tested. There remain no detections in poultry or in our agricultural production system. The risk to human health remains low. While tests are pending, local media is also reporting on a dead seal pup which washed up on the beaches of Warrnambool on Victoria's Southwest coast. There are, of course, other possible causes of death, but recent events make H5N1 a distinct possibility. The most recent national tally from the Australian Agriculture Dept. Detection of H5 bird flu As of 11am AEST, 6 August 2026, Australia has 123 confirmed detections of H5 bird flu in wild birds. 10 in Western Australia (WA) 87 in South Australia (SA) 2 in New South Wales (NSW) 1 in Queensland (QLD) 23 in Victoria (VIC). This is the serious H5 bird flu strain that has been circulating globally. There have been no detections in poultry or the wider agriculture industry. The Consultative Committee for Emergency Animal Disease (CCEAD) has reviewed its previous advice and endorsed a framework on national poultry biosecurity measures that will commence from 31 July. Under this framework, state and territory governments are responsible for issuing advice on biosecurity measures using a risk-based approach. State and territory governments are responsible for surveillance and response activities on the ground. They are actively working with industry to provide guidance on implementation of enhanced biosecurity measures, as appropriate. Find out more about bird flu in your state or territory. National coordination is being led by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF). The risk to human health remains low. Australia is well prepared to respond quickly. Update: FLI Detects Novel Orthobunyavirus in German/Swiss Dairy Cattle Biting Midge after blood meal #19,279 Four days ago we looked at a statement from the Swiss FSVO (Federal Office for Food Safety and Veterinary Affairs) on their Investigation into an Unidentified Bovine Disease which produced fevers, diarrhea, and substantial milk drop in dairy cows. Since then, Germany's FLI (Friedrich Loeffler Institute) has announced the results of their own investigation, which had discovered high levels of a novel orthobunyavirus of the Simbu serogroup present in affected cattle. Orthobunyaviruses are a large and growing family `arboviruses' - viruses carried and spread by biting insects (mosquitoes, ticks & midges) - that mostly infect animals, but are sometimes zoonotic. The virus in question is reportedly similar to viruses that are found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. These types of viruses are not usually zoonotic, but additional studies will be needed to determine its actual risk. I've posted the FLI press release below: FLI detects a new orthobunyavirus of the Simbu serogroup (“Shamonda-like”) in cattle in Germany 08/03/2026 Press Releases The Friedrich-Loeffler-Institut (FLI) has detected a previously uncharacterised orthobunyavirus of the Simbu serogroup in samples from affected cattle in southern Germany. Following the first appearance of the Schmallenberg virus in 2011, this once again provides reliable evidence that a new virus from this group has been introduced into Germany. The newly detected virus shows the closest relationship to the Shamonda virus in all three segments. Viruses of the Simbu serogroup are found primarily in Africa, Asia and Australia. Like bluetongue virus and Schmallenberg virus, they are transmitted by blood-sucking midges of the genus Culicoides. The animals most commonly infected are ruminants, particularly cattle, sheep and goats. Cases were first detected in cattle in Switzerland, France and southern Germany, particularly in Baden-Württemberg. The affected animals showed signs of fever and diarrhoea. In dairy cows, a decline in milk yield – in some cases significant – was also observed. These clinical signs have been observed in numerous animals and herds since July. The clinical signs were initially consistent with infection by the Schmallenberg virus. However, tests for Schmallenberg virus, as well as for other known pathogens such as bluetongue virus or epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus, proved negative. Samples from four affected cattle herds were submitted to the FLI by the local state veterinary laboratory (Chemisches und Veterinäruntersuchungsamt Freiburg). Within 48 hours, the samples had been analysed and the pathogen further characterised. A Pan-Simbuvirus PCR revealed clear positive signals in several serum and blood samples from different farms, with Ct values of up to around 20. This indicates high viral loads at the time of sampling. Further PCR tests for viruses in this group also yielded positive results. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that all three genome segments showed the highest sequence similarity to Shamonda viruses (at the amino acid level: S: 99 %; M: 95 %; L: 97 %). Whilst the S and L segments are also closely related to Schmallenberg virus, the M segment – which is particularly relevant for antigenicity and the immune response – shows a significantly lower degree of similarity (<50 %). The final taxonomic classification of the virus is currently pending. Infections with viruses of the Simbu serogroup generally lead to a brief period of viraemia and only mild to moderate clinical signs in adult animals. Of particular significance, however, is the potential transmission to the foetus during pregnancy. Depending on the timing of the infection, abortions, stillbirths and severe congenital malformations may occur. In the case of e Schmallenberg virus, sheep were particularly affected by this. In some flocks, malformation was observed in up to 50 % of the offspring. In cattle, foetal malformations were less pronounced. As regards the newly identified ‘Shamonda-like’ virus, it is not yet possible to assess whether, and to what extent, infections in pregnant animals may lead to malformation in the foetuses. Abortions, stillbirths and malformed calves or lambs from herds that may be affected should therefore be examined. Depending on the weather, the midge season in Germany lasts until around the end of November. Midge activity is usually at its peak between July and October. Given the generally efficient transmission by midges, a further and potentially rapid spread of the virus within susceptible herds is therefore anticipated. Viruses of the Simbu serogroup are not generally considered to be zoonotic agents and, based on current knowledge, do not pose a significant risk of infection to humans. However, in the case of newly emerging and insufficiently characterised viruses in this group, their potential zoonotic risk should be investigated as a precautionary measure and closely monitored as the situation develops. The FLI is giving high priority to the complete characterisation of the pathogen, the epidemiological tracing of cases, and the adaptation and development of specific diagnostic methods. “Following the 2011 Schmallenberg virus outbreak, an exotic orthobunyavirus has once again been introduced into Central Europe. Investigations over the coming weeks will reveal how rapidly it is spreading, which animal species are particularly affected, and what clinical consequences can be expected. Of crucial importance is the question of whether infections during pregnancy lead to foetal malformation,” said Prof. Dr. Martin Beer, Vice-President of the Friedrich-Loeffler-Institut. In principle, vaccines can be developed against orthobunyaviruses. However, this requires sufficient lead time. The necessity and urgency of vaccine development will depend largely on the clinical and, in particular, reproductive significance of the newly introduced virus. Precursors to the 2009 H1N1 pandemic virus, which emerged from North American pigs, appear to have been circulating for at least a decade before it began its world tour. It has been estimated that ancestral strains of COVID-19 may have been circulating for 4 to 7 decades in bats before spilling over into humans. We've been watching HPAI H5Nx for 3 decades, and while it continues to improve its game, it has yet to adapt well enough to human physiology to spread efficiently. The same could be said for many other novel viruses, including both swine and avian flu, henipaviruses like Nipah, scores of other coronaviruses, and of course `Disease X'; the placeholder for those threats yet to be discovered. One of the `usual suspects' we keep coming back to is LPAI H9N2, which is ubiquitous in Asian poultry, has spread to both Africa and the Middle East, and just recently turned up in Europe. While roughly 200 human (mostly mild) cases have been reported over the past 30 years - mostly from China - recently we've seen an uptick in cases, with 9 reported in China/Hong Kong over the past 2 months (see WHO WPRO Reporting 4 More H9N2 Cases on Chinese Mainland). Several recent studies have found signs that LPAI H9N2 is becoming better adapted to mammals, warning of its pandemic potential; including: Two months ago, in Viruses: Epidemiological and Virological Characteristics of H9N2 Avian Influenza Virus in Jiangsu Province, China, 2024, researchers warned that that Jiangsu’s circulating H9N2 viruses have acquired human receptor preference and mammalian adaptation, posing silent infection and pandemic risks Last October, in China CDC Weekly: Epidemiological and Genetic Characterization of Three H9N2 Viruses Causing Human Infections, investigators reported a number of indicators of increased mammalian adaptation within the virus, including an enhanced ability to infect upper respiratory (α2,6-sialic acid) tract receptors, and a number of HA protein mutations, including; H191N, A198V, Q226L, and Q234L. The Asian Y280/G57 lineages have shown increasing signs of mammalian adaptation (see EM&I: Enhanced Replication of a Contemporary Avian Influenza A H9N2 Virus in Human Respiratory Organoids)), while the African and Middle Eastern Lineages (mostly European G1-like) are older and less evolved. Last summer, in Nature: Genetic diversity of H9N2 avian influenza viruses in poultry across China and implications for zoonotic transmission, researchers reported rising prevalence of key mutations associated with increased infectivity and pathogenicity in mammals. Despite being clearly zoonotic - LPAI H9N2 is considered a `non-reportable' disease in poultry or wild birds by WOAH (see Terrestrial Animal Code). As a result, there are huge gaps in surveillance and reporting around the world. Complicating matters, China's attempts to control LPAI H9N2 through vaccines have been less than successful. In 2025's NPJ Vaccines: Impact of Inactivated Vaccine on Transmission and Evolution of H9N2 Avian Influenza Virus in Chickens, we saw evidence that inactivated vaccines failed to prevent - or even reduce - H9N2 in China's poultry, and may have driven viral evolution (including mammalian adaptations). All of which brings us to yet another Chinese study which - once again - finds that China's LPAI H9N2 continues to diversify and accrue worrisome mammalian adaptations, which they suggest increase its zoonotic risk. Due to its length and technical nature, I've only posted some excerpts from the abstract and narrative. Those looking for a deeper dive will want to follow the link to read it in its entirety. I'll have a brief postscript after the break. (SNIP) These mutations can increase the replication of H9N2 virus in mammalian cells and enhance the pathogenicity of the virus to mammals. In vitro replication experiments showed that the current H9N2 virus could replicate efficiently in MDCK, A549 and HBE cells, and the titer of CK225/22 was higher than that of the other strains. In vivo experiments showed that the current G57 and G118 genotype H9N2 viruses replicated effectively in the turbinate and lungs of mice and caused body weight loss. And many will be surprised to see that, in terms of risk of emergence, the H9N2 Y280 lineage is ranked higher than H5N1, while the G1 lineage is ranked only slightly lower. Given the paucity of day-to-day news coming out of China regarding avian flu, it is difficult to gauge just how much of threat H9N2 currently poses. But based on the frequency of Chinese studies published on LPAI H9 over the past couple of years, they quite obviously take its threat seriously. Which suggests we should, as well. Tuesday, August 04, 2026 Australia: H5N1 Positive Bird Detections (n=102) Continue to Rise #19,277 The number of confirmed H5N1 detections in wild birds in Australia has more than quintupled in a little over a week, rising from 20 on July 27th to 102 today (Aug 4th). Most of this increase has come from the state of South Australia, where the first mass mortality event (in birds) has been confirmed. Two quick updates this morning from the Australian Authorities, first this from DAFF. Attributable to Australian Chief Veterinary Officer, Dr Beth Cookson: Testing at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness (ACDP) has confirmed further positive results in South Australia, bringing the total to 81 in South Australia. This includes detections in Limestone Coast (Southend, Robe and Baudin Rocks), Kangaroo Island (Harriet River, Seal Bay, Vivonne Bay and D’Estrees Bay), Coorong, Glenelg, Troubridge Island and The Pages Islands. The Baudin Rocks detection follows an investigation into over 80 sick or dead wild birds, and is the first confirmed mass mortality event in wildlife in Australia due to H5 bird flu. title: Neuropathology, novel tissue tropism, and evidence of vertical transmission in South American pinnipeds naturally infected with high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 virus in Argentina.
abstract: In 2023, high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 outbreaks caused mass mortality events affecting pinnipeds throughout South America. Here, we present the clinical, pathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings associated with HPAI H5N1 infection in 3 South American sea lions ( Otaria flavescens ) and 1 southern elephant seal ( Mirounga leonina ) stranded during the outbreak in Chubut, Argentina. Neurological signs were observed in 2 sea lions, with 1 also exhibiting respiratory distress. Necropsies were conducted on all 4 animals. Neuropathology revealed mild-to-severe lymphohistiocytic (2/4) to mixed neutrophilic (2/4) meningoencephalitis with neuronal necrosis, neuronophagia, glial cell proliferation, multifocal hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing in all animals. Novel findings for HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds included choroid plexitis (2/4) and myelitis (2/4). Immunohistochemistry for viral nucleoprotein was positive in 3 of 4 animals and involved neurons (3/3), glial cells (3/3), and ependymal cells (2/3). Viral-related systemic findings included multifocal necrotizing myocarditis in the elephant seal and multifocal necrotizing placentitis in a sea lion, with HPAI virus detected within fetal tissues. Pulmonary lesions were minimal and were limited to multifocal necrosis of bronchial glands in 1 sea lion. HPAI H5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction and sequencing in all animals. These findings indicate a predominance of central nervous system involvement in HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds and expand the recognized spectrum of virus-associated lesions, identifying novel tissue tropisms and transmission routes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to address the severe impact of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 outbreaks on South American pinnipeds in 2023, which caused mass mortality events. The authors aimed to characterize the clinical, pathological, and molecular features of HPAI H5N1 infection in naturally infected pinnipeds to fill knowledge gaps about tissue tropism and transmission routes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined 4 pinnipeds—3 South American sea lions (Otaria flavescens) and 1 southern elephant seal (Mirounga leonina)—stranded during an HPAI H5N1 outbreak in Chubut, Argentina. Necropsies were conducted on all animals to assess clinical and pathological findings.
analysis.methods: HPAI H5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus infection was confirmed using polymerase chain reaction and sequencing in all animals. Neuropathological examination included assessment of meningoencephalitis, neuronal necrosis, glial cell proliferation, hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing.
analysis.main_results: Neuropathology revealed lymphohistiocytic to mixed neutrophilic meningoencephalitis with neuronal necrosis, neuronophagia, glial cell proliferation, multifocal hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing in all 4 animals. Immunohistochemistry detected viral nucleoprotein in neurons (3/3), glial cells (3/3), and ependymal cells (2/3). Novel findings included choroid plexitis (2/4) and myelitis (2/4). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate a predominance of central nervous system involvement in HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds and expand the recognized spectrum of virus-associated lesions. Novel tissue tropisms and transmission routes, including vertical transmission, were identified.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic approaches for HPAI H5N1 in marine mammals to inform conservation strategies and assess zoonotic risk. It underscores the importance of monitoring neurological and reproductive system involvement in affected species.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=4) and lack of control animals limit generalizability and the strength of causal inferences. The study relies on post-mortem examinations, which may not capture early or subclinical infections, and the findings are specific to a single outbreak location.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the neuropathology, tissue tropism, and transmission of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 in South American pinnipeds during a 2023 outbreak in Argentina. Necropsies of 3 South American sea lions and 1 southern elephant seal revealed consistent central nervous system involvement, including meningoencephalitis, neuronal necrosis, and glial cell proliferation, alongside novel findings such as choroid plexitis and myelitis. Viral nucleoprotein was detected in neurons, glial cells, and ependymal cells via immunohistochemistry. Systemic lesions included myocarditis and placentitis, with evidence of vertical transmission in one case. The authors conclude that HPAI H5N1 in pinnipeds exhibits a predominance of neurological involvement and previously unrecognized tissue tropisms. The findings emphasize the need for targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies in marine mammals to inform conservation and public health measures.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study examined 4 pinnipeds—3 South American sea lions (Otaria flavescens) and 1 southern elephant seal (Mirounga leonina)—stranded during an HPAI H5N1 outbreak in Chubut, Argentina. analysis_en.methods: HPAI H5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus infection was confirmed using polymerase chain reaction and sequencing in all animals. Neuropathological examination included assessment of meningoencephalitis, neuronal necrosis, glial cell proliferation, hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing.
analysis_en.main_results: Neuropathology revealed lymphohistiocytic to mixed neutrophilic meningoencephalitis with neuronal necrosis, neuronophagia, glial cell proliferation, multifocal hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing in all 4 animals. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate a predominance of central nervous system involvement in HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds and expand the recognized spectrum of virus-associated lesions. Novel tissue tropisms and transmission routes, including vertical transmission, were identified.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic approaches for HPAI H5N1 in marine mammals to inform conservation strategies and assess zoonotic risk. title_zh: 阿根廷自然感染高致病性 禽流感 H5N1 病毒的南美鳍足类动物的神经病理学、新组织向性和垂直 传播 的证据。
source_body_en: In 2023, high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 outbreaks caused mass mortality events affecting pinnipeds throughout South America. Here, we present the clinical, pathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings associated with HPAI H5N1 infection in 3 South American sea lions ( Otaria flavescens ) and 1 southern elephant seal ( Mirounga leonina ) stranded during the outbreak in Chubut, Argentina. Neurological signs were observed in 2 sea lions, with 1 also exhibiting respiratory distress. Necropsies were conducted on all 4 animals. Neuropathology revealed mild-to-severe lymphohistiocytic (2/4) to mixed neutrophilic (2/4) meningoencephalitis with neuronal necrosis, neuronophagia, glial cell proliferation, multifocal hemorrhage, and perivascular cuffing in all animals. Novel findings for HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds included choroid plexitis (2/4) and myelitis (2/4). Immunohistochemistry for viral nucleoprotein was positive in 3 of 4 animals and involved neurons (3/3), glial cells (3/3), and ependymal cells (2/3). Viral-related systemic findings included multifocal necrotizing myocarditis in the elephant seal and multifocal necrotizing placentitis in a sea lion, with HPAI virus detected within fetal tissues. Pulmonary lesions were minimal and were limited to multifocal necrosis of bronchial glands in 1 sea lion. HPAI H5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction and sequencing in all animals. These findings indicate a predominance of central nervous system involvement in HPAI H5N1-infected pinnipeds and expand the recognized spectrum of virus-associated lesions, identifying novel tissue tropisms and transmission routes.

title: D347G in PA is critical for the pathogenicity of H9N2 avian influenza A virus in mice.
abstract: ABSTRACT Some subtypes of avian influenza A viruses (IAVs) have been associated with human infections (e.g. H3N8, H5Ny, H7Ny, H9N2, and H10Ny), and the ability of these viruses to cause zoonotic infections further increases the public health risk of avian IAVs. Among them, H9N2 virus is one of particular importance, both in its own right and as a contributor of internal gene segments to other emerging zoonotic avian IAVs. In recent years, an increasing number of H9N2 strains have been observed to be highly pathogenic in mice without prior adaptation. In this study, we found that a naturally occurring H9N2 isolate, A/chicken/Jiangxi/198/2019 (JX198), is lethal in mice. To investigate the molecular basis for the high virulence of JX198 in mice, a series of reassortants and mutants were generated and tested. We found that the PA, especially D347G mutation in PA, is responsible for the increased pathogenicity of JX198 in mice. Notably, D347G in PA of JX198 significantly alters the polymerase activity, vRNA production, and plaque-formation. Thus, our data demonstrate that a novel molecular marker, D347G in PA, determines the virulence of H9N2 in mice, posing a potential risk of H9N2 with D347G in PA for public health and highlighting the significance of continuing surveillance of H9N2 field strains.

title: Subclass switching enhances protective efficacy of a non-neutralizing H7N9 avian influenza antibody.
abstract: Non-neutralizing antibodies contribute to protection against the H7N9 subtype avian influenza virus through Fc effector functions. Antibody subclass plays a critical role in determining binding affinity to Fc receptors (FcR) and downstream Fc effector functions. In this study, to assess whether antibody subclass switching can enhance antibody protective efficacy, subclass of a non-neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) against the hemagglutinin of H7N9 virus was switched from IgG1 to IgG2a, and their activity and protective efficacy were assessed. Subclass switching caused no significant changes in antigen binding, hemagglutination-inhibition and virus neutralizing activities of the antibody. The hybridoma-derived mAb conferred no protection against H7N9 virus infection. Interestingly, both IgG2a and IgG1 antibodies produced in CHO cells provided full protection against mortality caused by a sublethal H7N9 virus challenge. Upon lethal challenge, IgG2a antibody conferred 70% protection, whereas its IgG1 counterpart only provided 30% protection. However, both antibodies did not decrease virus loads in mouse lungs. Moreover, compared to the IgG1 antibody, affinity of the subclass-switched IgG2a antibody to FcR was significantly increased, as evidenced by enhanced binding of the antibody to recombinant murine FcγRI and to FcRs on murine macrophages. Our findings highlighted a benefit of subclass-engineering to antibody modification and development of therapeutic antibodies.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study assessed the activity and protective efficacy of a non-neutralizing mAb against H7N9 hemagglutinin after switching its subclass from IgG1 to IgG2a, using hybridoma-derived and CHO cell-produced antibodies in mouse models challenged with H7N9 virus.
analysis.methods: The subclass of a non-neutralizing mAb against H7N9 hemagglutinin was switched from IgG1 to IgG2a, and antigen binding, hemagglutination-inhibition, virus neutralizing activities, Fc receptor binding affinity, and protective efficacy were evaluated in mouse challenge models.
analysis.main_results: Subclass switching did not alter antigen binding, hemagglutination-inhibition, or virus neutralizing activities, but IgG2a showed significantly higher affinity to FcγRI and murine macrophage FcRs compared to IgG1. In sublethal challenge, both IgG1 and IgG2a provided full protection, whereas in lethal challenge, IgG2a conferred 70% protection versus 30% for IgG1. Neither antibody reduced virus loads in mouse lungs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that subclass switching enhanced protective efficacy by improving Fc receptor engagement without altering antigen-binding or neutralizing activity, highlighting a novel strategy for therapeutic antibody engineering against H7N9.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that subclass engineering of therapeutic antibodies could improve clinical outcomes for H7N9 infections by enhancing Fc-mediated protection, informing future vaccine and therapeutic development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to mouse models and did not evaluate virus load reduction or long-term protection, which constrains generalizability to human infections; the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human data and mechanistic depth.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether switching the subclass of a non-neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) against H7N9 avian influenza virus from IgG1 to IgG2a could enhance its protective efficacy. The authors found that subclass switching did not alter antigen binding, hemagglutination-inhibition, or virus neutralizing activities but significantly increased Fc receptor binding affinity. In mouse challenge models, both IgG1 and IgG2a provided full protection against sublethal H7N9 infection, while IgG2a conferred 70% protection compared to 30% for IgG1 in lethal challenge. Neither antibody reduced virus loads in lungs. The authors concluded that subclass engineering enhances Fc-mediated protection without compromising antigen specificity, offering a novel approach for therapeutic antibody development against H7N9.

title_zh: 亚类转换增强非中和性 H7N9 禽流感 抗体的保护功效。
source_body_en: Non-neutralizing antibodies contribute to protection against the H7N9 subtype avian influenza virus through Fc effector functions. Antibody subclass plays a critical role in determining binding affinity to Fc receptors (FcR) and downstream Fc effector functions. In this study, to assess whether antibody subclass switching can enhance antibody protective efficacy, subclass of a non-neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) against the hemagglutinin of H7N9 virus was switched from IgG1 to IgG2a, and their activity and protective efficacy were assessed. Subclass switching caused no significant changes in antigen binding, hemagglutination-inhibition and virus neutralizing activities of the antibody. The hybridoma-derived mAb conferred no protection against H7N9 virus infection. Interestingly, both IgG2a and IgG1 antibodies produced in CHO cells provided full protection against mortality caused by a sublethal H7N9 virus challenge. Upon lethal challenge, IgG2a antibody conferred 70% protection, whereas its IgG1 counterpart only provided 30% protection. However, both antibodies did not decrease virus loads in mouse lungs. Moreover, compared to the IgG1 antibody, affinity of the subclass-switched IgG2a antibody to FcR was significantly increased, as evidenced by enhanced binding of the antibody to recombinant murine FcγRI and to FcRs on murine macrophages. Our findings highlighted a benefit of subclass-engineering to antibody modification and development of therapeutic antibodies.
abstract_zh: 非中和抗体通过 Fc 效应子功能有助于抵御 H7N9 亚型 禽流感 病毒。抗体亚类在确定与 Fc 受体 (FcR) 的结合亲和力和下游 Fc 效应子功能方面发挥着关键作用。在本研究中,为了评估抗体亚型转换是否可以增强抗体的保护功效,将针对H7N9病毒血凝素的非中和性单克隆抗体(mAb)亚型从IgG1转换为IgG2a,并评估其活性和保护功效。亚类转换不会导致抗体的抗原结合、血凝抑制和病毒中和活​​性发生显着变化。杂交瘤衍生的 mAb 不能提供针对 H7N9 病毒感染的保护作用。有趣的是,CHO 细胞中产生的 IgG2a 和 IgG1 抗体都提供了针对亚致死 H7N9 病毒攻击引起的 死亡率 的全面保护。在致死攻击后,IgG2a 抗体提供 70% 的保护,而其 IgG1 抗体仅提供 30% 的保护。然而,这两种抗体都没有减少小鼠肺部的病毒载量。此外,与 IgG1 抗体相比,亚类转换 IgG2a 抗体对 FcR 的亲和力显着增加,如该抗体与重组鼠 FcγRI 和鼠巨噬细胞上 FcR 的结合增强所证明。我们的研究结果强调了亚类工程对抗体修饰和治疗性抗体开发的好处。

title: A One-Shot Multivalent Live-Attenuated Candidate Influenza Vaccine against Divergent Zoonotic H5N1 Clades
abstract: Abstract The continued emergence of genetically diverse high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 viruses with zoonotic potential highlights the urgent need for developing vaccines capable of providing broad protection against multiple circulating clades. Here, we developed a one-shot, multivalent, live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) based on the temperature-sensitive (ts), cold-adapted (ca), and attenuated ( att ) influenza A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 master donor virus (MDV) that incorporates the hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) glycoproteins from representative clades 2.3.4.4b (A/Louisiana/12/2024), 2.3.2.1a (A/Victoria/149/2024), and 2.3.2.1e (A/Cambodia/2302009/2023) H5N1 viruses. A single intranasal (IN) immunization of C57BL/6 mice with the multivalent LAIV elicited robust humoral immune responses, with immune sera exhibiting broad cross-reactivity against antigens from all three H5N1 clades included in the vaccine. Following homologous viral challenge, vaccinated C57BL/6 mice were completely protected from disease, demonstrating the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the multivalent LAIV. By simultaneously targeting antigenically distinct H5N1 lineages with pandemic potential, this strategy expands antigenic coverage within a single LAIV to confirm pan-H5N1 protection. Together, these findings support the development and implementation of this multivalent LAIV as a broadly protective pan-H5N1 LAIV for pandemic preparedness. Significance The increasing genetic diversity of zoonotic H5N1 viruses complicates vaccine design. We developed a multivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) based on the temperature-sensitive, cold-adapted, and attenuated ( ts , ca , att ) master donor virus (MDV) influenza A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 backbone that expresses the hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) glycoproteins of H5N1 clades 2.3.4.4b, 2.3.2.1a, and 2.3.2.1e. A single intranasal (IN) immunization with the multivalent LAIV induced broadly cross-reactive neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses and protected experimental vaccinated animals against homologous lethal viral challenge, demonstrating the feasibility of the multivalent LAIV to protect against H5N1 clades of highest concern to humans. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing and implementing this multivalent LAIV as a broad protective pan-H5N1 LAIV against divergent H5N1 viruses for human use.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the urgent public-health need for vaccines that can protect against genetically diverse zoonotic H5N1 influenza viruses, which continue to emerge in multiple clades and pose pandemic risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed a multivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) using the ts/ca/att A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 backbone expressing HA and NA from H5N1 clades 2.3.4.4b, 2.3.2.1a, and 2.3.2.1e, and evaluated it in C57BL/6 mice.
analysis.methods: A single intranasal dose of the multivalent LAIV was administered to mice, and immune sera were assessed for cross-reactivity against clade-matched antigens; protection was evaluated after homologous lethal challenge.
analysis.main_results: Vaccinated mice showed robust humoral responses with broad cross-reactivity against all three H5N1 clades and were completely protected from disease following homologous challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating the feasibility of a single-shot multivalent LAIV that expands antigenic coverage across antigenically distinct H5N1 lineages, representing a novel pan-H5N1 strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support advancing this multivalent LAIV as a broadly protective pan-H5N1 vaccine candidate for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a mouse model and lacks human data, which constrains generalizability and necessitates cautious interpretation of the strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a one-shot multivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) using a temperature-sensitive, cold-adapted A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 backbone expressing hemagglutinin and neuraminidase from three divergent H5N1 clades (2.3.4.4b, 2.3.2.1a, 2.3.2.1e). In C57BL/6 mice, a single intranasal immunization induced broadly cross-reactive neutralizing antibodies and conferred complete protection against homologous lethal challenge. The authors conclude that this multivalent LAIV strategy expands antigenic coverage within a single vaccine and demonstrates feasibility as a pan-H5N1 vaccine candidate for pandemic preparedness. However, the evidence is confined to a mouse model and lacks human data, limiting generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究满足了公共卫生对 疫苗 的迫切需求,该药物可以预防基因多样化的人畜共患 H5N1 流感病毒,这些病毒继续在多个分支中出现并构成大流行风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作者使用表达 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b、2.3.2.1a 和 2.3.2.1e 的 HA 和 NA 的 ts/ca/att A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 主干开发了多价减毒活流感 疫苗 (LAIV),并在 C57BL/6 小鼠中进行了评估。
elements_zh.methods: 对小鼠进行单次鼻内剂量的多价 LAIV,并评估免疫血清与进化枝匹配抗原的交叉反应性;在同源致死攻击后评估保护作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 接种疫苗的小鼠表现出强烈的体液反应,对所有三个 H5N1 进化枝具有广泛的交叉反应性,并且在同源攻击后完全免受疾病影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了单次多价 LAIV 的可行性,该疫苗可以扩大抗原覆盖范围,覆盖不同抗原的 H5N1 谱系,代表了一种新的泛 H5N1 策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持将这种多价 LAIV 作为一种具有广泛保护性的泛 H5N1 疫苗 候选药物,用于大流行防范。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于小鼠模型,缺乏人类数据,这限制了普遍性,并且需要谨慎解释证据的强度。

title: Deciphering viral action on host genome structure: a computational physics perspective.
abstract: Recent experimental findings indicate that several viruses are able to substantially re-organize the host cell genome architecture. Since chromatin three-dimensional (3D) organization is tightly linked to vital cellular functions, investigating how viral infections impact physical mechanisms shaping DNA folding provides useful clues about virus action on gene regulation and consequent activation. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the development of computational modelling approaches used to shed light on how host cell chromatin 3D structure is altered following viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2 and avian influenza IAV-H5N1. Given the flexibility of this approach, such models can be adapted to a wide range of pathogens, making them valuable methods for investigating the specificity of distinct infection mechanisms. Overall, we show how such models can be helpful tools that, in tandem with traditional experimental methods, allow to decipher complexity of infection mechanisms at molecular level from a new perspective.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on avian influenza A viruses, specifically examining how these viruses alter the host cell genome structure through computational modeling approaches. The central question is how viral infections impact the physical mechanisms that shape DNA folding, offering insights into gene regulation and activation.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of computational modeling approaches used to study the effects of avian influenza A viruses on host chromatin 3D structure. It includes studies on SARS-CoV-2 and avian influenza IAV-H5N1, highlighting the flexibility of these models in adapting to various pathogens.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that computational models are effective tools for understanding how avian influenza A viruses reorganize the host genome. These models, when combined with traditional experimental methods, provide a new perspective on deciphering the molecular complexity of infection mechanisms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that while computational models offer valuable insights, they may not fully capture the nuances of viral interactions with host DNA. There is a need for more detailed studies on the specific mechanisms of avian influenza subtypes, particularly in diverse host populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research should focus on refining computational models to better reflect the biological specificity of avian influenza subtypes. It also emphasizes the importance of integrating these models with experimental data to improve understanding and inform public health strategies.

title: CD4 + T-cell responses directed towards A/H5N1-derived haemagglutinin peptides increase in patients with seasonal influenza A virus infection.
abstract: Abstract Objectives Recent outbreak of influenza A/H5N1 viral infections in birds and mammals worldwide prompted renewed concerns over an emerging H5N1‐related influenza pandemic in the generally immunologically‐naive global population. Cross‐reactive CD4+ T cells between A/H1N1 and A/H5N1 subtypes targeting internal and surface influenza proteins have been identified in humans, indicating some protection against severe and fatal A/H5N1 infection. Methods To detect T‐cell responses towards H1 and H5 viruses, we stimulated PBMCs from patients hospitalised with seasonal influenza A viruses, alongside healthy individuals, with overlapping peptide pools spanning hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) of A/Vietnam/1203/2004 (H5N1) and A/New York/18/2009 (H1N1‐pdm09‐like) viruses. Results Majority of acutely infected and healthy participants (100% and 75%, respectively) had detectable CD4+ and CD8+ T‐cell responses towards H1‐HA and H5‐HA, whereas 30–80% of individuals had detectable H5‐NA responses. H1 and H5 HA‐specific CD4+ T‐cell responses highly correlated, suggesting some level of cross‐reactivity between T‐cell responses directed against H1 and H5 subtypes. HA‐specific CD4+ T‐cell responses were increased in influenza patients compared to healthy participants. We found no differences in H1‐ and H5‐specific T cell responses between those born pre‐ and post‐1968, irrespective of infection status. Sequence alignment of H1 and H5 viruses identified high conservation in the HA2 stalk subunit (81.53%). CD4+ T‐cell immunity towards immunodominant HA306–318 epitope, restricted by several HLA‐DRB1 molecules, revealed limited cross‐reactivity between Group 1 and Group 2 HA‐subtypes. Conclusion We define correlative H1‐ and H5‐specific CD4+ T‐cell responses during seasonal influenza A virus infection, likely reflecting some level of H1/H5 T cell cross‐reactivity.

source_records.abstract: Objectives Recent outbreak of influenza A/H5N1 viral infections in birds and mammals worldwide prompted renewed concerns over an emerging H5N1-related influenza pandemic in the generally immunologically-naive global population. Cross-reactive CD4 + T cells between A/H1N1 and A/H5N1 subtypes targeting internal and surface influenza proteins have been identified in humans, indicating some protection against severe and fatal A/H5N1 infection. Methods To detect T-cell responses towards H1 and H5 viruses, we stimulated PBMCs from patients hospitalised with seasonal influenza A viruses, alongside healthy individuals, with overlapping peptide pools spanning hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) of A/Vietnam/1203/2004 (H5N1) and A/New York/18/2009 (H1N1-pdm09-like) viruses. Results Majority of acutely infected and healthy participants (100% and 75%, respectively) had detectable CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell responses towards H1-HA and H5-HA, whereas 30-80% of individuals had detectable H5-NA responses. H1 and H5 HA-specific CD4 + T-cell responses highly correlated, suggesting some level of cross-reactivity between T-cell responses directed against H1 and H5 subtypes. HA-specific CD4 + T-cell responses were increased in influenza patients compared to healthy participants. We found no differences in H1- and H5-specific T cell responses between those born pre- and post-1968, irrespective of infection status. Sequence alignment of H1 and H5 viruses identified high conservation in the HA2 stalk subunit (81.53%). CD4 + T-cell immunity towards immunodominant HA 306-318 epitope, restricted by several HLA-DRB1 molecules, revealed limited cross-reactivity between Group 1 and Group 2 HA-subtypes. Conclusion We define correlative H1- and H5-specific CD4 + T-cell responses during seasonal influenza A virus infection, likely reflecting some level of H1/H5 T cell cross-reactivity.

title_original: CD4 + T-cell responses directed towards A/H5N1-derived haemagglutinin peptides increase in patients with seasonal influenza A virus infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether cross-reactive CD4+ T-cell responses exist between seasonal influenza A/H1N1 and avian A/H5N1 viruses in humans, motivated by global concerns over potential H5N1 pandemics in immunologically naive populations following recent outbreaks in birds and mammals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study enrolled patients hospitalized with seasonal influenza A virus infection and healthy individuals, collecting peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess T-cell responses against hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) peptides from A/H5N1 and A/H1N1 viruses.
analysis.methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were stimulated with overlapping peptide pools spanning HA and NA proteins from A/Vietnam/1203/2004 (H5N1) and A/New York/18/2009 (H1N1-pdm09-like) viruses to detect CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses using standard immunological assays.
analysis.main_results: All acutely infected participants and 75% of healthy participants had detectable CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses to H1-HA and H5-HA, while 30–80% showed detectable H5-NA responses; HA-specific CD4+ T-cell responses were higher in influenza patients than in healthy participants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the strong correlation between H1- and H5-HA-specific CD4+ T-cell responses as evidence of cross-reactivity, noting high conservation in the HA2 stalk subunit (81.53%) and limited cross-reactivity at the immunodominant HA306–318 epitope across HA subtypes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that pre-existing CD4+ T-cell immunity from seasonal influenza may provide partial protection against severe H5N1 infection, informing future vaccine strategies targeting conserved HA regions to broaden influenza immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size, lack of direct H5N1 infection cases, and reliance on in vitro peptide stimulation assays, which may not fully reflect in vivo immune responses, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated cross-reactive CD4+ T-cell responses between seasonal influenza A/H1N1 and avian A/H5N1 viruses in humans, prompted by global concerns over potential H5N1 pandemics. Using PBMCs from hospitalized seasonal influenza patients and healthy controls, the authors detected CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses to H1-HA and H5-HA in all acutely infected participants and 75% of healthy individuals, with higher HA-specific CD4+ T-cell responses in infected patients. Responses to H5-NA were detectable in 30–80% of participants. The study identified high conservation in the HA2 stalk subunit (81.53%) and strong correlation between H1- and H5-HA-specific CD4+ T-cell responses, suggesting cross-reactivity. However, limited cross-reactivity was observed at the immunodominant HA306–318 epitope across HA subtypes. These findings imply that pre-existing CD4+ T-cell immunity from seasonal influenza may confer partial protection against severe H5N1 infection, offering insights for vaccine design targeting conserved HA regions. The evidence is moderate due to small sample size, absence of direct H5N1 infection cases, and reliance on in vitro assays.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了人类季节性流感 A/H1N1 和禽类 A/H5N1 病毒之间是否存在交叉反应性 CD4+ T 细胞反应,其动机是全球对最近鸟类和哺乳动物 暴发 后免疫学幼稚人群中潜在的 H5N1 大流行的担忧。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究招募了因季节性甲型流感病毒感染住院的患者和健康个体,收集外周血单核细胞 (PBMC),以评估 T 细胞针对 A/H5N1 和 A/H1N1 病毒的血凝素 (HA) 和神经氨酸酶 (NA) 肽的反应。
elements_zh.methods: 使用跨越 A/Vietnam/1203/2004 (H5N1) 和 A/New York/18/2009 (H1N1-pdm09-like) 病毒的 HA 和 NA 蛋白的重叠肽池刺激外周血单核细胞 (PBMC),以使用标准免疫测定法检测 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有急性感染参与者和 75% 的健康参与者对 H1-HA 和 H5-HA 都有可检测到的 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞反应,而 30-80% 则表现出可检测到的 H5-NA 反应;流感患者的 HA 特异性 CD4+ T 细胞反应高于健康参与者。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 H1-和 H5-HA 特异性 CD4+ T 细胞反应之间的强相关性解释为交叉反应性的证据,并指出 HA2 茎亚基 (81.53%) 的高度保守性和跨 HA 亚型的免疫显性 HA306-318 表位的有限交叉反应性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对季节性流感的现有 CD4+ T 细胞免疫可能对严重 H5N1 感染提供部分保护,为未来针对保守 HA 区域的 疫苗 策略提供信息,以扩大流感免疫力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小、缺乏直接H5N1感染病例以及依赖体外肽刺激测定的限制,这可能无法完全反映体内免疫应答,需要谨慎地将证据强度解释为中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 最近全球范围内鸟类和哺乳动物中发生的 A/H5N1 流感病毒感染事件再次引发人们对在全球普遍免疫学上未接受过免疫的人群中出现的新出现的 H5N1 相关流感大流行的担忧。已在人类体内发现了针对内部和表面流感蛋白的 A/H1N1 和 A/H5N1 亚型之间的交叉反应性 CD4+ T 细胞,这表明对严重和致命的 A/H5N1 感染有一定的保护作用。方法 为了检测针对 H1 和 H5 病毒的 T 细胞反应,我们刺激了因季节性甲型流感病毒住院的患者以及健康个体的 PBMC,其中包含 A/Vietnam/1203/2004 (H5N1) 和 A/New York/18/2009(H1N1-pdm09-like)病毒的血凝素 (HA) 和神经氨酸酶 (NA) 重叠肽库。结果 大多数急性感染者和健康参与者(分别为 100% 和 75%)对 H1-HA 和 H5-HA 具有可检测到的 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞反应,而 30-80% 的个体具有可检测到的 H5-NA 反应。H1 和 H5 HA 特异性 CD4+ T 细胞反应高度相关,表明针对 H1 和 H5 亚型的 T 细胞反应之间存在一定程度的交叉反应。与健康参与者相比,流感患者的 HA 特异性 CD4+ T 细胞反应增强。我们发现,无论感染状态如何,1968 年之前和之后出生的人的 H1 和 H5 特异性 T 细胞反应没有差异。H1 和 H5 病毒的序列比对发现 HA2 茎亚基具有高度保守性 (81.53%)。CD4+ T 细胞对免疫显性 HA306-318 表位的免疫,受到几个 HLA-DRB1 分子的限制,揭示了第 1 组和第 2 组 HA 亚型之间有限的交叉反应性。结论 我们定义了季节性甲型流感病毒感染期间相关的 H1 和 H5 特异性 CD4+ T 细胞反应,可能反映了一定程度的 H1/H5 T 细胞交叉反应性。

title: Spatio-temporal Modelling of H5N1 Avian Influenza Outbreaks in Europe (2021-2024)
abstract: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), particularly the H5N1 strain, poses a significant ongoing threat to animal health, biodiversity and food security across Europe. Understanding where and when avian influenza risks intensify is essential for targeted surveillance and rapid response. This study develops a data-driven spatio-temporal framework that integrates geospatial, ecological and climatic datasets to explain and forecast the dynamics of H5N1 outbreaks between 2021 and 2024. analysis.research_question_and_background: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1 continues to threaten animal health, biodiversity and food security across Europe, creating an urgent need to understand where and when risks intensify for targeted surveillance and rapid response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a data-driven spatio-temporal framework integrating geospatial, ecological and climatic datasets to explain and forecast H5N1 outbreaks in Europe between 2021 and 2024, using weekly country-level outbreak counts from 37 countries over 208 weeks.
analysis.methods: Weekly country-level outbreak counts were analysed using a hierarchical endemic-epidemic model with a Negative Binomial distribution, incorporating environmental covariates, bird-species densities and human population metrics into endemic and autoregressive components.
analysis.main_results: The endemic-epidemic model outperformed a regression-only Negative Binomial baseline by reducing mean logS by approximately 29% and RPS by 49%, with improved probabilistic calibration and high forecast accuracy (RPS = 0.76, logS = 0.61).

analysis.summary_en: This study addressed the urgent need to understand and forecast H5N1 avian influenza outbreaks in Europe (2021–2024) by developing a spatio-temporal framework that integrates geospatial, ecological and climatic datasets. Using weekly country-level outbreak counts from 37 countries over 208 weeks, the authors applied a hierarchical endemic-epidemic model with Negative Binomial distribution, incorporating environmental covariates and bird-species densities. The model substantially outperformed a regression-only baseline, reducing mean logS by 29% and RPS by 49%, with high forecast accuracy (RPS = 0.76, logS = 0.61). Findings indicate transmission is driven by ecological drivers and local persistence, with Anseriformes, Charadriiformes and Pelecaniformes densities identified as key contributors. The framework offers a scalable approach for early-warning systems in HPAI surveillance, though reliance on aggregated data and model assumptions limits generalisability and evidence strength to moderate.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) continues to cause substantial mortality in poultry and wild birds globally [1,2]. The study aimed to investigate whether the seasonality of HPAI is changing over time.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed global HPAI surveillance data from multiple regions to assess seasonal patterns. It included data from poultry and wild bird populations across different geographic locations.
analysis.methods: The researchers reviewed and analyzed HPAI surveillance data to identify seasonal trends. They compared historical data with recent observations to determine if there was a shift in seasonality.
analysis.main_results: Previously, HPAI showed marked winter seasonality.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that the observed changes in seasonality may indicate a shift in the epidemiology of HPAI, potentially affecting surveillance and control strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of more effective surveillance and response strategies for HPAI outbreaks, particularly in regions where seasonal patterns are changing.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on historical data and does not include detailed statistical analysis, which may limit the confidence in its conclusions. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether the seasonality of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is changing globally. It reviews historical and recent surveillance data to assess seasonal patterns in poultry and wild bird populations. The results indicate that HPAI previously showed marked winter seasonality, but there is a suggestion of a shift in its epidemiology. The authors interpret this as a potential change in the virus's behavior, which could have implications for surveillance and control strategies. However, the study's reliance on observational data without detailed statistical analysis limits the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 继续在家禽中造成大量 死亡率,并在全球范围内造成 野生鸟类 [1,2]。该研究旨在调查高致病性禽流感的季节性是否随时间而变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了来自多个地区的全球 HPAI 监测 数据,以评估季节性模式。它包括来自不同地理位置的家禽和 野生鸟类 种群的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员审查并分析了 HPAI 监测 数据,以确定季节性趋势。他们将历史数据与最近的观察结果进行比较,以确定是否存在季节性变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 此前,HPAI表现出明显的冬季季节性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,观察到的季节性变化可能表明 HPAI 的 流行病学 发生了变化,可能会影响 监测 和控制策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于制定更有效的 监测 和 HPAI 暴发 应对策略,特别是在季节性模式发生变化的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于历史数据,不包括详细的统计分析,这可能会限制其结论的可信度。由于分析的观察性质,证据的强度中等。

title: Comparative Immunogenicity of Inactivated H7N9 Avian Influenza Vaccines with Different Internal Gene Backbones
abstract: H7N9 avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a persistent threat to poultry and public health. Despite widespread vaccination in China, rapid antigenic drift and reassortment necessitate frequent updates of vaccine strains. Phylogenetic analysis of isolates from Chinese provinces (from 2019 to 2023) showed that while surface genes diversified, the internal gene cassette remained conserved yet actively reassorted with other subtypes, suggesting internal gene compatibility may influence vaccine performance. We selected the H7N9 strain A/chicken/Northeast China/19854-6/2019 (E2), which harbors a polybasic Hemagglutinin (HA) cleavage site and predicted dual receptor-binding affinity. To enable safe vaccine development, we modified the HA cleavage site to generate a low-pathogenicity strain (E2-Δ). Using reverse genetics, we constructed three recombinant viruses: E2-Δ (retaining contemporary internal genes), CVI-E2, and CVII-E2 (containing internal genes from commercially used donor strains CVI and CVII, respectively). Inactivated vaccines were evaluated in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens. E2-Δ induced HI antibody titers comparable to those of CVI-E2 and significantly higher than those of CVII-E2, and showed modestly higher cross-reactive HI titers against some recent H7N9 variants in exploratory analyses. All vaccines provided complete homologous protection with reduced viral shedding and no clinical signs in challenge trials. Our findings suggest that internal gene backbone compatibility may influence vaccine immunogenicity. While E2-Δ outperformed CVII-E2, it was comparable to CVI-E2, indicating that certain traditional backbones may still be suitable for H7N9 vaccine development. This approach warrants further validation to support a refined vaccine design strategy for H7N9 and potentially other avian influenza subtypes.

abstract_zh: H7N9 禽流感 病毒 (AIV) 对家禽和公共卫生构成持续威胁。尽管疫苗接种在中国广泛传播,但快速的抗原漂移和重配使得疫苗毒株的频繁更新成为必要。对中国各省分离株(2019年至2023年)的系统发育分析表明,虽然表面基因多样化,但内部基因盒仍然保守,但与其他亚型积极重配,表明内部基因兼容性可能影响疫苗的性能。我们选择了 H7N9 毒株 A/鸡/中国东北/19854-6/2019 (E2),其具有多元血凝素 (HA) 裂解位点并预测了双重受体结合亲和力。为了实现 疫苗 的安全开发,我们修改了 HA 裂解位点以生成低致病性菌株 (E2-Δ)。利用反向遗传学,我们构建了三种重组病毒:E2-Δ(保留当代内部基因)、CVI-E2和CVII-E2(分别包含来自商业使用的供体菌株CVI和CVII的内部基因)。在无特定病原体 (SPF) 鸡中评估了灭活的 疫苗。E2-Δ 诱导的 HI 抗体滴度与 CVI-E2 相当,并且显着高于 CVII-E2,并且在探索性分析中针对最近的一些 H7N9 变种表现出略高的交叉反应 HI 滴度。所有 疫苗 均提供完整的同源保护,减少病毒脱落,并且在挑战试验中没有临床症状。我们的研究结果表明,内部基因主链兼容性可能会影响 疫苗 的免疫原性。虽然 E2-Δ 的性能优于 CVII-E2,但与 CVI-E2 相当,表明某些传统骨架可能仍然适合 H7N9 疫苗 的开发。这种方法需要进一步验证,以支持 H7N9 和潜在其他 禽流感 亚型的改进 疫苗 设计策略。

title: High pathogenicity avian influenza A (H5N1) viruses isolated from poultry and wild birds in Japan during the 2024–2025 season
abstract: ABSTRACT H5N1 high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b continue to spread globally among wild birds and poultry, and diversify through gene reassortment. Since 2024, spillovers of H5N1 viruses have been reported in dairy cattle in the United States. Given the numerous HPAI outbreaks in poultry and wild birds in Japan during the 2024–2025 season, we aimed to examine the genetic diversity, pathogenicity, and host range of these viruses. Phylogenetic analyses revealed that all viruses in the 2024–2025 season belonged to G2d and G2c subgroups in clade 2.3.4.4b and were divided into 11 genotypes (G2d: six genotypes, G2c: five genotypes). Of these, G2d-0 was the dominant genotype in both poultry and wild birds. Novel genotypes emerged through reassortment between G2d and G2c viruses. Experimental infection of chickens revealed comparable pathogenicity among genotypes, although the amounts of viral shedding were high in chickens inoculated with G2d-0 and G2c-13 viruses, which were genotypes confirmed in multiple outbreaks in the 2024–2025 season, suggesting high transmission potential. In vitro assays revealed markedly lower infectivity of Japanese isolates in bovine mammary epithelial cells compared with that of the B3.13 genotype responsible for dairy cattle outbreaks in the United States, indicating limited risk of cattle infection. Together, these findings underscore ongoing genetic diversification of HPAI viruses in G2d and G2c subgroups and highlight the importance of continued in vivo and in vitro characterization of these viruses to monitor changes in genotypes, pathogenicity, and potential risk of spillover to cattle. IMPORTANCE H5N1 high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses have spread in poultry and wild birds worldwide. H5N1 viruses have also spread in dairy cattle in the United States since 2024. Japan reported numerous HPAI cases during the 2024–2025 season. Herein, phylogenetic analyses using strains isolated from poultry and wild birds enabled a detailed investigation of their genetic backgrounds, which is essential for elucidating introduction routes and evolution. Investigation of pathogenicity may help predict the outbreak frequency. This study revealed that HPAI viruses of multiple genotypes had been introduced into Japan, and chickens infected with genotypes detected from continuous outbreaks exhibited high virus shedding. In addition, comparing infectivity in bovine cells revealed the risk of cattle infection. H5N1 infection had not been reported in cattle in Japan, and our results suggest that the risk remains low. These integrated analyses provide key insights for developing effective strategies against HPAI outbreaks.

title: Avian influenza risk mapping in India using machine learning
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) remains a recurrent threat to poultry production and One-Health surveillance in India. We developed a national relative spatial risk map for India using curated outbreak records spanning January 2006 to April 2024 (predominantly HPAI H5N1 and H5N8), buffered pseudo-absence sampling, H3 resolution-7 hexagons, and 94 environmental, livestock, land-cover, and anthropogenic predictors. Under 5-fold spatial block cross-validation, eight base classifiers were trained and all performed above chance (AUC > 0.76). The Gaussian-process stacked meta-learner achieved the highest AUC (0.853), but the improvement over the strongest individual base learner, Random Forest (AUC 0.851; Brier 0.155; ECE 0.079), was small and statistically non-significant. Its principal added value was a companion uncertainty layer, the GPR posterior standard deviation, which showed internal consistency with ensemble disagreement across base models ( r = 0.74, p < 0.001). Feature attribution ranked human population density, extensive chicken density, June precipitation, and seasonal humidity variables among the predictors most associated with model outputs, with interpretation constrained by passive-surveillance bias and multicollinearity. title: Validation of sample pooling for high-throughput RT-qPCR subtyping of avian influenza A(H5)
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) is a global health threat due to its high historical virulence and increasing mammalian host range, as demonstrated by the 2024–2025 outbreak among U.S. dairy cattle, with 71 confirmed human infections. While human-to-human transmission has not yet been documented, limited pre-existing human immunity, and uncertainty about evolutionary barriers to human infection make H5N1 a potential pandemic threat. Expanding testing capacity for H5N1 beyond its currently limited scope would be critical for response to potential outbreaks. Thus, we developed and validated a dual-target reverse transcription PCR assay for H5 subtyping of pooled influenza A-positive samples. The assay targets two regions of the hemagglutinin (HA) gene of influenza A(H5). Using contrived samples containing inactivated bovine H5N1 virus, we determined the assay’s 95% lower limit of detection for individual samples (58 copies/mL; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 50 to 66 copies/mL) and eight-sample pools (2,465 copies/mL; 95% CI: 1,969 to 3,756 copies/mL). The assay demonstrated 100% positive percent agreement, detecting H5 in all contrived H5-positive pools (32/32 pools; 95% CI: 89.1% to 100.0%) where the contrived positive samples ranged from 500,000 to 3,906 copies/mL. We observed 100% negative percent agreement in H5-negative, influenza A-positive pools (32/32; 95% CI: 89.1% to 100.0%). Though sample pooling reduced analytical sensitivity, contrived samples with H5 virus present at levels typically found in human respiratory infections were detected in eight-sample pools. This approach has the potential to increase testing capacity for influenza A (H5) while maintaining adequate sensitivity, enhancing preparedness for potential outbreaks. IMPORTANCE Avian influenza A(H5N1) poses a potential pandemic threat. H5N1 testing capacity is currently limited. We validated an influenza A (H5) subtyping RT-qPCR for testing pooled samples to increase capacity. The assay displays adequate analytical sensitivity to detect clinical respiratory infections based on prior human cases. This proactive assay validation enhances outbreak preparedness.
